body:
I was browsing through some Unabomber book and the author is some fancy
forensic pathologist or something, and the book analyzed the varioius
pieces of evidence in the case, including the faint impression of a note
someone had written on top of the wrapping paper the Unabomber used that
simply read "call Nathan R Wed 7 pm."

The lofty forensic psychologist then proceeds to analyze the handwriting
and proceeds the brand the writer as emotionally immature and hates
social situations among other very detailed assumptions about whoever
wrote it.  First of all, I find it very difficult to believe that any
headfucker could glean all that from a scrawled telephone note, and of
course the book was written AFTER Ted was busted, so the headfucker's
handwriting analysis is meaningless.

But what I never found out is whether the Nathan R note was ever proven
to have been written by Ted.  TK was so clever he would often throw in
fake evidence to confuse the feds; for example, he enjoyed collecting
tree twigs in his various travels across the country and would include
one with the bomb so that the feds would be all over Kentucky or
wherever the tree is found, while Ted was actually making and mailing
them far away, or he would pick up stray hairs in public restrooms and
toss those in.  He was so careful to never leave any trace of himself on
his bombs, everything was wiped clean and of course he threw in false
clues too.  So why would he be so careless as to write a note on top of
the carefully-wrapped package he had spent months preparing?

Did the feds determine who Nathan R was and his connection to TK?  Did
they ever explain why someone with no telephone would scrawl what
appears to be a telephone message on top of his precious bomb?  Is this
lofty forensic behavioral psychologist (a profession St. Ted expressed
particular disgust of) really able to analyze a person's entire life
just from 5 words on a telephone note or is he just full of shit?

Real quick, psychologists are headfuckers, about as useful as Dr. Phil.
If fact, you really don't even need a Ph.D., anyone who watches an
episode of Dr. Phil becomes qualified to make psychological assessments.

My favorite psychologist is that one who testified at the Andrea Yates
trial, that she was faking it because he had seen an episode of "Law &
Order" where a mother killed her children then faked insanity.  Using a
television show as evidence to support your professional opinion is bad
enough, but then it turns out the episode never even existed.  But
because he had watched an episode of Dr. Phil he was qualified to offer
testimony that could result in the defendant's death.

----------------------------------------------
"Just think, an irresponsible genetic engineer
might create a lot of terrorists."
-- The Gospel of St. Ted
